clinician.final_diagnosis: Abdominal tuberculosis (TB) with mesenteric lymph node involvement, confirmed by M. tuberculosis PCR in mesenteric lymph node biopsy
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old female housekeeper from Bangladesh presented in September 2022 with a 2-month history of right-sided abdominal pain that worsened after meals, accompanied by diarrhea, bloating, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and 5 kg weight loss. Physical examination revealed a distended abdomen with palpable bowel loops and increased bowel sounds; rectal examination was normal. Initial laboratory workup showed anemia (Hb 10.30 g/dL), leukocytosis (WBC 14.35×10^9/L), elevated ESR, and positive H. pylori infection. Chest X-ray and upper abdominal ultrasound were normal. CT abdomen/pelvis demonstrated distended ileum with fecal matter, dilated jejunal and ileal loops, minimal free fluid adjacent to the terminal ileum, and reduced caecal caliber with prominent submucosal fat and diffuse postcontrast mucosal enhancement in the caecum and ascending colon, initially raising suspicion for inflammatory bowel disease. Endoscopic biopsy of the ileum and cecum revealed granulomatous inflammation with focal chronic active disease. Mesenteric lymph node biopsy was subsequently performed, and M. tuberculosis was identified by PCR, confirming the diagnosis of abdominal TB. The patient was initiated on antituberculous therapy with documented clinical improvement, including symptom resolution, weight gain, and increased strength. She remained under outpatient follow-up and maintained clinical improvement despite a concurrent SARS-CoV-2 infection during treatment, which resolved within 72 hours.

final.final_diagnosis: Abdominal tuberculosis (TB) with mesenteric lymph node involvement, confirmed by M. tuberculosis PCR in mesenteric lymph node biopsy
final.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old female housekeeper from Bangladesh presented in September 2022 with a 2-month history of right-sided abdominal pain that worsened after meals, accompanied by diarrhea, bloating, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and 5 kg weight loss. Physical examination revealed a distended abdomen with palpable bowel loops and increased bowel sounds; rectal examination was normal. Initial laboratory workup showed anemia (Hb 10.30 g/dL), leukocytosis (WBC 14.35×10^9/L), elevated ESR, and positive H. pylori infection. Chest X-ray and upper abdominal ultrasound were normal. CT abdomen/pelvis demonstrated distended ileum with fecal matter, dilated jejunal and ileal loops, minimal free fluid adjacent to the terminal ileum, and reduced caecal caliber with prominent submucosal fat and diffuse postcontrast mucosal enhancement in the caecum and ascending colon, initially raising suspicion for inflammatory bowel disease. Endoscopic biopsy of the ileum and cecum revealed granulomatous inflammation with focal chronic active disease. Mesenteric lymph node biopsy was subsequently performed, and M. tuberculosis was identified by PCR, confirming the diagnosis of abdominal TB. The patient was initiated on antituberculous therapy with documented clinical improvement, including symptom resolution, weight gain, and increased strength. She remained under outpatient follow-up and maintained clinical improvement despite a concurrent SARS-CoV-2 infection during treatment, which resolved within 72 hours.
